answer: An astronomy job market can stop free aliases from dominating bids for nebula, spiral galaxy and comet labels by requiring a work ticket per bid. Each ticket is a hash puzzle bound to the job ID, bidder key and a fresh round nonce; the market records spent tickets so they cannot be replayed. Selection counts valid tickets, never account totals, and there is no signup bonus. A thousand bids therefore cost a thousand puzzles regardless of aliases. Adjust difficulty to keep flooding expensive, while recognizing that large computing farms still have an advantage.
